carbonic-maceration.definition: A process beginning with intact whole bunches in a closed, oxygen-excluding carbon-dioxide atmosphere, with intracellular metabolism before pressing and fermentation completion.
carbonic-maceration.matters: It is a mechanism, not an appellation rule or a complete cellar recipe.

elevage.definition: The raising of a wine between fermentation and bottling: time, vessel, topping and other cellar choices all live inside it.
elevage.matters: Here it separates time in barrel from bottle age.

flor.definition: A film-forming yeast layer that develops on a wine's surface under the right cellar conditions.
flor.matters: It can shape aroma and structure more strongly than the grape name does.

foehn.definition: A warm, dry downslope wind. In Jurançon it can interrupt the wet Atlantic pattern during the long autumn ripening season.
foehn.matters: It helps explain concentration and drying conditions without pretending the foothills are generally arid.

marl.definition: A clay-rich calcareous rock or sediment; Jura growers often distinguish its bands, ages and colors.
marl.matters: It is useful site context, not a flavor guarantee.

mistelle.definition: A sweet wine made by adding spirit to grape must before or during early fermentation.
mistelle.matters: Macvin belongs to this family; it is not another name for vin jaune.

nouveau.definition: A regulated early-release mention—also called primeur—currently available to qualifying red and rosé Beaujolais, not white.
nouveau.matters: It shaped global recognition without ever accounting for all Beaujolais production.

ouille.definition: Topped up: the barrel is refilled as wine evaporates, keeping headspace and oxygen contact low.
ouille.matters: It is the most useful word for avoiding the idea that every Jura white is oxidative.

passerillage.definition: Concentration as grapes lose water and shrivel, usually while remaining on the vine in this Jurançon context.
passerillage.matters: It is a ripening and concentration path, not another word for botrytis.

sec.definition: Dry. In this appellation the word is part of the legal name Jurançon sec and corresponds to a maximum fermentable-sugar threshold.
sec.matters: A bottle labeled only Jurançon is not the dry category.

semi-carbonic.definition: A related process in which ordinary fermentation of released juice can create carbon dioxide around intact berries in a whole-bunch vat.
semi-carbonic.matters: It does not require the same deliberately established external-CO₂ atmosphere as full carbonic maceration.

sous-voile.definition: Under a yeast veil: wine ages without regular topping while a film-forming yeast layer develops on its surface.
sous-voile.matters: This is biological ageing, not simple neglect and not a grape flavor.

tries-successives.definition: Successive picking passes through the vineyard, selecting fruit as it reaches the intended maturity or concentration.
tries-successives.matters: The current rule requires this repeated selection for Jurançon other than the sec path.

vendanges-tardives.definition: Late harvest, used here as a regulated Jurançon mention with its own grape, harvest-date and sugar requirements.
vendanges-tardives.matters: It is a narrower legal path than simply harvesting ripe fruit late.

voile.definition: Literally ‘veil’: the film of yeast that can form over wine in a partly filled vessel.
voile.matters: The veil creates a biological pathway distinct from ordinary oxygen exposure.

whole-cluster.definition: Fermentation that includes intact bunches and stems.
whole-cluster.matters: Whole cluster describes grape handling; it does not prove that a ferment is carbonic or semi-carbonic.

place:saumur-wine-region.thesis: Saumur deserves its own component: two core legal areas, two major grape routes and a human story in which Clos Rougeard's 2017 acquisition and Collier's family work line must stay distinct.

place:touraine-wine-region.hero_kicker: Opposite banks · plural grapes · work and family routes
place:touraine-wine-region.thesis: Touraine is not a midpoint. Vouvray, Montlouis, Chinon, Cheverny and Cour-Cheverny keep legal place and grape roles separate, while Huet and Tue-Boeuf open different human explanations.

place:vallee-du-loir.hero_kicker: Loir, not Loire · two AOPs · a succession route
place:vallee-du-loir.thesis: Jasnières, Coteaux du Loir, Pineau d’Aunis and Bellivière make the tributary branch structurally necessary. It is not filler between Touraine and the larger regional story.

comparison.detail: Intact whole bunches begin in a closed, oxygen-excluding CO₂ atmosphere; pressing and ordinary fermentation completion follow.
comparison.label: Carbonic

comparison.detail: Fermenting juice in a whole-bunch vat can generate CO₂ around intact berries without a fully established external-CO₂ treatment.
comparison.label: Semi-carbonic

comparison.detail: Intact bunches and stems enter the vessel; that handling choice alone proves neither carbonic nor semi-carbonic fermentation.
comparison.label: Whole cluster
comparison.value: Fruit handling, not the whole mechanism

featured_connections.reason: See why a whole-bunch vat generating its own CO₂ is related to—but distinct from—full carbonic maceration.
Intact bunches describe material entering the vessel, not the complete fermentation mechanism.
A current producer protocol makes externally established CO₂ conditions concrete without universalizing them.

practice:carbonic-maceration.hero_kicker: A process word that says less than many drinkers think

practice_examples.label: Lapierre
practice_examples.text: Current first-party practice names semi-carbonic maceration, indigenous yeasts, barrel completion and selective—not universally absent—sulfur.

practice_examples.label: Grand’Cour
practice_examples.text: Current estate material explicitly describes uncrushed, undestemmed bunches in CO₂-saturated tanks: a producer-specific full-carbonic example.

practice_examples.label: Terres Dorées
practice_examples.text: A 2024 operating transition means any inherited cellar shorthand must be dated rather than silently projected onto the current operation.

practice:carbonic-maceration.thesis: {{term:carbonic-maceration|Carbonic maceration}}, {{term:semi-carbonic|semi-carbonic maceration}} and {{term:whole-cluster|whole-cluster fermentation}} answer different questions. Added CO₂, intact bunches, yeast source, extraction, élevage and sulfur remain separate dimensions—and Beaujolais law does not impose one universal recipe.

practice:ouillage.thesis: {{term:ouille|Ouillé}} means topped up. In Jura it is the word that keeps grape identity from being confused with an oxidative cellar path.

practice:semi-carbonic-maceration.hero_kicker: Related to carbonic · not a synonym
practice:semi-carbonic-maceration.thesis: In a whole-bunch vat, ordinary fermentation of released juice can generate CO₂ around intact berries. That mixed mechanism differs from a fully established external-CO₂ treatment, and a regional tradition does not make it a universal legal requirement.

practice:sous-voile-aging.thesis: {{term:sous-voile|Sous voile}} is a biological ageing pathway under a yeast veil. It is not shorthand for every Jura white—or for simple oxidation.

practice:whole-cluster-fermentation.hero_kicker: A handling choice · not a complete fermentation diagnosis
practice:whole-cluster-fermentation.thesis: Whole cluster means intact bunches and stems enter the fermenter. To call the process carbonic or semi-carbonic, you still need evidence about atmosphere and fermentation—not a guess from the stem decision.

producer:camin-larredya.hero_kicker: Jurançon · terraces and a four-grape estate mix
producer:camin-larredya.thesis: Camin Larredya makes scope visible: a 9.5-hectare certified-organic estate, four hectares of terraces, a local four-grape mix—and separately identified purchased fruit rather than one blurred domaine story.

producer:chateau-thivin.hero_kicker: Odenas · family continuity on the Mont Brouilly route
producer:chateau-thivin.thesis: Château Thivin makes Mont Brouilly human through Geoffray family tenure from 1877 and a current focus on Côte de Brouilly and Brouilly. It is essential precisely because Beaujolais history is larger than the natural-wine frame.

producer:clos-du-tue-boeuf.hero_kicker: Les Montils · transmission without a school
producer:clos-du-tue-boeuf.thesis: Tue-Boeuf connects family estate, organic farming, purchased fruit, Menu Pineau and a documented work/partnership route through Pierre-Olivier Bonhomme. It does not turn producer practice into Touraine law or every bottle into Vin de France.

then_now.intro: A durable producer identity can cross a material ownership change.

now.label: NOW · current estate
now.text: The Bouygues family has owned Clos Rougeard since 2017 and the estate presents a current team preserving its identity.

then.label: THEN · Foucault family era
then.text: Eight generations culminated publicly in the Foucault brothers before the 2017 acquisition.

then_now.title: Continuity is not unchanged ownership

producer:clos-rougeard.thesis: Clos Rougeard links Cabernet Franc and Chenin to a long Foucault history, then marks a 2017 acquisition. Domaine du Collier is a family/work branch, not the same producer after succession.

producer:clos-uroulat.thesis: Clos Uroulat’s current visitor range makes a useful correction: Jurançon can be read across dry, tender and sweet positions instead of as a single binary switch.

producer:coulee-de-serrant.thesis: La Coulée de Serrant connects Chenin, a specific legal origin, a dated biodynamic conversion and the 2001 organization. Atlas keeps producer, appellation, advocacy and attributed philosophy as four different objects.

producer:domaine-alexandre-bain.hero_kicker: Pouilly · a control dispute, not a tasting legend

then_now.intro: The claim is limited to the documented habilitation period.

now.label: MAY 2017 · remedy
now.text: The Dijon administrative court restored Bain's AOC rights.

then.label: SEPTEMBER 2015 · withdrawal
then.text: INAO withdrew habilitation on the stated basis of a required-control dispute.

then_now.title: Two dates replace one viral myth

producer:domaine-alexandre-bain.thesis: Bain's 2015–17 case establishes a mandatory-control dispute and a court remedy. Farming philosophy may be relevant producer context, but it is not the proven legal cause and later classifications require separate wine/vintage evidence.

producer:domaine-cauhape.hero_kicker: Monein · slope, altitude and stylistic range
producer:domaine-cauhape.thesis: Domaine Cauhapé is a scale-and-range anchor: southeast-facing Monein slopes rising toward 400 metres, with dry and sweet wines held in the same estate frame.

producer:domaine-de-la-grand-cour.hero_kicker: Fleurie · named sites and an explicit CO₂ protocol
producer:domaine-de-la-grand-cour.thesis: Grand’Cour makes producer specificity do the teaching: a Fleurie history across named sites and a current whole-bunch protocol in CO₂-saturated tanks. Neither the site names nor the cellar method become a regional universal.

featured_connections.reason: The bottle-level proof that Savagnin can be deliberately topped and non-oxidative.
Move from one wine to the grape's wider set of cellar paths.
The domaine's Arbois base opens the legal and geographic layer behind the bottle.

producer:domaine-de-la-tournelle.hero_kicker: Arbois · a cellar decision made legible
producer:domaine-de-la-tournelle.thesis: Évelyne and Pascal Clairet's domaine makes a useful teaching move: Fleur de Savagnin has been a topped expression since the 1990s, so the grape never has to stand in for oxidation.

featured_connections.reason: A recurring Arbois white whose documented composition changes by vintage—a useful check on fixed bottle assumptions.
Follow Château Renard outward to the geographic AOP that classifies it.
Use the documented 2018 bottling as one specific route into Jura Chardonnay.

producer:domaine-de-saint-pierre-jura.hero_kicker: Mathenay · a contemporary estate in motion
producer:domaine-de-saint-pierre-jura.thesis: Fabrice Dodane's Domaine de Saint Pierre adds a contemporary Mathenay perspective: certified organic farming and a recurring Arbois white whose composition needs to be read vintage by vintage.

producer:domaine-de-souch.hero_kicker: Laroin · small scale and patient work
producer:domaine-de-souch.thesis: Domaine de Souch brings the world down to human scale: seven hectares, three local grapes, organic farming, biodynamic principles and manual harvest.

producer:domaine-des-terres-dorees.hero_kicker: Charnay · southern Beaujolais in a live transition

then_now.intro: This is an operating-role transition, not evidence of a sale or retirement.

now.label: NOW · announced transition
now.text: Domaines Roger Zannier holds operation and development, while the announcement keeps Brun involved in a five-year wine-focused transition.

then.label: THEN · before harvest 2024
then.text: The domaine’s public identity centered on Jean-Paul Brun before the new operating arrangement began.

then_now.title: A current producer identity can change without becoming a clean succession myth

producer:domaine-des-terres-dorees.thesis: Terres Dorées holds together southern geography, a source-described Chardonnay area and a 2024 operating transition in which Jean-Paul Brun remains involved. Atlas preserves the source’s unresolved total-acreage arithmetic instead of manufacturing precision.

featured_connections.reason: A Chardonnay route under veil beside a domaine known for topped whites.
A multi-parcel Savagnin route that refuses the single-vineyard assumption.
Chardonnay becomes a site and cellar instrument rather than a generic white-grape card.

producer:domaine-labet.thesis: Domaine Labet is most useful as a parcel-and-process laboratory: topped whites, a documented sous-voile Chardonnay, and a family estate spread across 45 parcels.

producer:domaine-marcel-lapierre.hero_kicker: Morgon · transmission, cellar precision and succession
producer:domaine-marcel-lapierre.thesis: The useful Lapierre story is specific: Marcel’s documented 1981 turn under Jules Chauvet’s guidance, organic certification, current semi-carbonic work, selective sulfur use and a family operation now co-owned by Mathieu and Camille.

producer:domaines-landron.hero_kicker: Pays Nantais · farming change with dates
producer:domaines-landron.thesis: Landron's first-party chronology makes a durable Muscadet door: family continuity, a 1987 soil-work turn, organic conversion from 1999 and later biodynamic certification. None becomes a Muscadet rule or an origin myth.

producer:jean-foillard.hero_kicker: Villié-Morgon · an individual beyond the shorthand
producer:jean-foillard.thesis: Foillard’s Morgon and Côte du Py associations make a strong place route. The evidence supports Chauvet influence, not an invented formal mentorship, and the map point remains municipality-level orientation rather than vineyard holdings.

featured_connections.reason: The current maker's apprenticeship and 2001 handoff turn ‘influence’ into a human chronology.
The earlier chapter: family vines, a 1968 start, and a handoff that kept the elder present.
Leave the cult object behind and return to the grape and its several possible endings.

producer:maison-pierre-overnoy.hero_kicker: Pupillin · a house, people, and a handoff

lenses.text: Most regular cuvées share a front label. Wax color, bottle size and the small bottling date are practical identity clues—not a collecting game.
lenses.title: Read the wax, then read the wine

lenses.text: Extreme US allocation pressure is real and market-specific. It explains why the bottle becomes a status signal; it does not make that bottle necessary for learning the work.
lenses.title: Scarcity can crowd out the lesson

producer:maison-pierre-overnoy.thesis: Read the handoff, not the hype. Pierre Overnoy and Emmanuel Houillon matter as a story of work, transmission and patience before they matter as scarce labels.

featured_connections.reason: The project becomes concrete in its Palomino Fino solera wine.
Follow Palomino beyond one project and one regional name.

project:soleras-del-pacifico.hero_kicker: Wine project · a California flor experiment
project:soleras-del-pacifico.thesis: Soleras del Pacífico is a project-shaped subject: a maker, an old Contra Costa planting and a solera practice converging in one wine.

wine:domaine-de-la-tournelle-fleur-de-sa.thesis: One wine that corrects a regional shortcut: 100% Savagnin, grey {{term:marl|marl}}, deliberately {{term:ouille|ouillé}} and non-oxidative.

wine:domaine-labet-chardonnay-du-hasard.hero_kicker: A specific expression · Chardonnay under veil
wine:domaine-labet-chardonnay-du-hasard.thesis: A useful false friend: the grape is Chardonnay, while the most recognizable signal comes from 36–48 months {{term:sous-voile|sous voile}}.

featured_connections.reason: Move from one California solera wine into Palomino's wider naming and place world.
The producer project behind the solera, vineyard choice and flor pathway.

wine:flor-of-evangelho.thesis: The Flor of Evangelho turns an analogy into a bottle: Palomino Fino, an old Contra Costa site, light fortification, fractional blending and ageing under flor.
